inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-06-30: 2,705.04m shares in issue (H1 FY2026 interim) less 83.88m repurchased in H1 but not yet cancelled = 2,621.16m, plus 24.57m dilutive RSUs from the H1 FY2026 EPS note = 2,645.7m. Shares held by the RSU nominee are not deducted (conservative). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; the RMB300m buyback is the cash mechanism, not modelled as accretion.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual cash flow statement 'Share-based payment expense' RMB28,541k (1951.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:6049); equals the 'Amortization ESOP costs' add-back in the adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation. No equity-award tax withholding line (HK RSU scheme settled from nominee-held shares).

Cross-check via USD legs at the same date: HKD=X 7.8479 / CNY=X 6.6768 = 1.1754 (0.26% tie), direction confirmed (HKD per CNY). All flows and per-share values computed in RMB and multiplied by fx_rate for the HKD quote; no dual listing exists for a direct parity check.
inputs.wacc_rationale: RMB-built. Cost of equity = China 10y CGB ~1.9% + beta 1.2 x 7.0% China ERP (incl. country risk) = ~10.3%. After-tax cost of debt = 3.61% weighted bank-borrowing rate (H1 FY2026 note 20) x (1-25%) = ~2.7%. Market weights at the current price: equity ~RMB4.95bn vs bank debt RMB2.48bn (~67/33) -> ~7.8%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: China demand, US execution and impairment risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not as a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash (principal + interest; FY2025 RMB66.4m + RMB24.2m = 3.4% of revenue, FY2024 4.0%, H1 FY2026 3.5%) is charged via lease_cost_pct_path inside EBIT; lease liabilities (RMB412.3m at 2026-06-30) are EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is bank borrowings only (RMB738.9m current + RMB1,743.0m non-current). da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (~2% of revenue removed) so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is small (RMB56.9m equity at 2026-06-30; H1 FY2026 NCI profit RMB3.0m). Flows are consolidated; NCI deducted once at book value in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF per .claude/skills/dcf-methods (operating company: private IVF/ARS hospital operator in China plus HRC Medical in the US and PT Morula in Indonesia), with the non-US adaptations (RMB flows / HKD quote, IFRS-16 leases, NCI). First valuation; no prior DCF or memory entry. Base year normalisation: FY2025 statutory EBITDA (-RMB565.9m) includes RMB998.6m goodwill/intangible impairment (HRC US and Laos), RMB99.0m ECL impairment and a RMB50m one-off contribution; the component build therefore anchors on company adjusted EBITDA (FY2023 RMB781.2m / 28.0%, FY2024 RMB707.3m / 25.2%, FY2025 RMB491.1m / 18.5%, H1 FY2026 RMB336.5m / 24.5%), not statutory figures. Adjusted EBITDA adds back ESOP cost, so it is pre-SBC; SBC is charged separately. Impairments are non-cash and do not enter the flows; their only lasting effect is that the RMB992.6m write-off is evidence of past overpayment, reflected in the bear case. Interest income not stripped: the company is net debt (RMB1.72bn), not net cash. Buybacks: a repurchaser (FY2025 RMB90.7m; H1 FY2026 RMB165.6m / HK$189.2m for 83.9m shares; up to RMB300m programme), so the flat share count is being funded. Working capital set to zero capture: payables (RMB758m) exceed receivables + inventory (RMB325m) and patients largely prepay per cycle, but construction payables dominate the balance and are not a growth-linked inflow. Debt reconstruction flagged by the parser does not affect inputs here: total_debt is read directly from the H1 FY2026 bank-borrowings note (RMB2,481,865k, line 3773), with no subtotal reconstruction.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 5yr CAGR 13.2% vs equity 5yr 4.7%: the revenue CAGR is acquisition-driven (HRC US, Wuhan, Kunming) and equity is depressed by the FY2025 RMB992.6m impairment; organic growth is closer to the 3yr revenue CAGR of 3.9%.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs not meaningful (FY2025 EPS negative on impairment). Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC; interest income not stripped as the company is net debt): FY2020 14.8, FY2021 195.3, FY2022 -450.7 (Shenzhen/Chengdu capex RMB959m), FY2023 466.9, FY2024 319.6, FY2025 309.2. 3yr and 5yr CAGRs are undefined (negative / near-zero start); FY2021-FY2025 4yr CAGR 12.2%. Owner-FCF CAGR is not below reported FCF CAGR in a meaningful way - SBC has fallen from 5.9% of revenue (FY2020) to 1.1% (FY2025).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 6% from H1 FY2026 +6.6% (overseas +22.8%, Chengdu cycles -5.4%); FY2027 6.5% as Shenzhen Zhongshan (3x capacity, trial operation Feb 2026) and SB 729 ramp; fading to 3% as China demographics bind.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA margin 24.5% in H1 FY2026 vs 18.5% FY2025 trough and 25-28% FY2023-24; recovers to 26%, below the FY2023 peak given IOT/MSA fee decline and US physician cost.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 includes Shenzhen completion and final payments (H1 RMB101m) against <RMB50m new capex guidance; then ~5.5% maintenance, rising to match D&A ex-ROU at terminal.
base.cash_tax_rationale: Cash tax / PBT ran 33-35% FY2023-24 (PRC 25%, US, non-deductible items, dividend WHT); on an EBIT base (pre-interest) ~30%, easing to 28%.

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2025 loss was a one-time write-down of legacy M&A, not an earnings break: H1 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin is back at 24.5% and revenue grew 6.6%. China cycle volumes stay flat-to-down (Chengdu -5.4% in H1) as record-low births and weak consumer confidence offset gradual medical-insurance inclusion of ARS, while the US (HRC, SB 729 commercial-insurance mandate from January 2026) and the 3x-capacity Shenzhen Zhongshan hospital carry mid-single-digit group growth for five years before fading to 3%. Capex discipline (<RMB50m new capex guided for 2026) lifts owner FCF toward a ~10-11% margin.
scenario_narratives.bull: SB 729 converts into sustained double-digit US growth as group plans renew through 2026-27 and HRC reaches ~40 physicians by 2027; Shenzhen fills toward its capacity as the Greater Bay Area 'southern headquarters'; China's expanding insurance coverage and childcare subsidies lift ARS penetration from ~10.5% toward developed-market levels, and VIP / PGT (third-generation IVF, +72.8% in FY2025) mix pushes adjusted EBITDA margin back above the FY2023 28% level. Group revenue grows high-single to ~10% through FY2030.
scenario_narratives.bear: China demand keeps eroding: births continue to fall, provincial insurance reimbursement is set low enough to pull patients toward public hospitals that are adding capacity, and IOT/MSA management fees keep declining. US growth disappoints as SB 729 is interpreted narrowly and physician recruitment costs stay high, and the FY2025 impairment proves not to be the last (Laos, other overseas assets). Group revenue grows ~2%, adjusted EBITDA margin stays near the FY2025 trough at ~21%, and capex stays above maintenance to keep new capacity competitive.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: China IVF demand is structurally pressured by births and a single regulator controls licensing and reimbursement, the balance sheet carries RMB2.5bn of bank debt (net debt ~3.5x FY2025 adjusted EBITDA), and the RMB992.6m impairment shows acquisition overpayment. Base 50% as H1 FY2026 already confirms margin recovery. Bull cut to 25% because it needs SB 729, Shenzhen fill-up and China penetration gains to all go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Normalised owner-FCF DCF in RMB, converted to HKD at the spot CNY/HKD rate. The FY2025 impairment is excluded from the base as non-cash and non-recurring; the base year is anchored on company adjusted EBITDA cross-checked against the H1 FY2026 recovery. Leases are charged as operating cash cost (treatment B) and excluded from net debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: China ARS cycle volumes (Chengdu -5.4% in H1 FY2026) and the national birth trend
Pace and generosity of China medical-insurance reimbursement for ARS
California SB 729 conversion into profitable US volume at HRC Medical
Further impairment of overseas assets and capital-allocation discipline
Leverage: RMB2.48bn bank debt against ~RMB0.5-0.7bn adjusted EBITDA; refinancing cost
CNY/HKD rate: IV in HKD moves one-for-one with the RMB
